growthProgram.eyebrow: Startups, small businesses and established businesses ready for the next step
growthProgram.title: The Growth Program
growthProgram.body: You know your business. What's harder to know is where the next stage of growth is actually coming from, and whether what you're doing now is getting you there. The Growth Program answers that. We work with you to find your best opportunities, rank them by value, and build a plan you own. Four ways in, from do-it-yourself to fully done-for-you.
growthProgram.fitNote: Right for you if you're a founder or owner who wants to be sure the next move is the right one.

hero.title: The right team around every job.
hero.paraA: The United Republic is an independent Australian strategy and growth advisory, working with government and major brands through Strategic Advisory, and with owner-led businesses through The Growth Program.
hero.paraB: We help you define the real problem, shape the response, and stay involved through delivery.

james.title: Principal Consultant
james.name: James Trebilcock
james.bioA: Twenty-five years across strategy, communications, engagement, customer experience and operational leadership. For Toyota, Ford, Commonwealth Bank, Australia Post, DFAT Smartraveller, the Electoral Commission of South Australia and dozens of others. Campaigns that have reached millions of Australians.
james.bioB: The work has always been the same shape: find the real problem before anyone spends money on the wrong one. Understand what behaviours need to change. Build a strategy that connects insight, message and delivery, then make sure it survives contact with the real world.
james.bioC: The questions that helped grow national businesses and campaigns that influenced millions of Australians are the same questions that need to be asked of any-sized business. The scale changes. The quality of the thinking shouldn't.

tailoredTeam.title: No fixed team. No payroll to feed.
tailoredTeam.paraA: The United Republic doesn't run a permanent team or push work through a machine that needs feeding. Each project gets the specialists it actually needs: research, strategy, technology, trainers, creative, media, content, production, delivery, all selected because they're right for the job, not because they're already on the books.
tailoredTeam.paraB: You get senior thinking that isn't biased toward a particular channel, and specialist execution without the overhead.

whatChanges.title: The plan matters. The certainty matters more.
whatChanges.paraA: Owners tell us the tangible results first: spend stops leaking, decisions get faster, the priorities are finally on one page. But the thing they mention last is the thing they value most. They stop second-guessing. They walk into their own business on Monday knowing why they're doing what they're doing, and able to say so to their team, their partner and themselves.
whatChanges.paraB: That's the real product. Growth is the receipt.

centralIdea.title: Assumptions are costing you money.
centralIdea.paraA: Every business runs on assumptions. Why customers buy. Which work is most valuable. Where growth will come from. Some of them are right. Some are about the business, not the customer. Some are old wives' tales that have never been checked.
centralIdea.paraB: The problem isn't having assumptions. It's spending real money on them without knowing which are which.
centralIdea.paraC: The Growth Program replaces assumptions with evidence and insight. That's where better decisions, stronger margins and clearer priorities come from. Not from doing more. From knowing more.
centralIdea.quote: A stronger business isn't just about having more customers. It's about finding the right customers and focusing on the opportunities that will drive the growth you want. When you understand your objectives, the value of your customers and where to focus, you get clearer commercial choices and the ability to keep growing.
centralIdea.quoteAttribution: James Trebilcock, Founder, The United Republic

howItWorks.title: Five stages. One plan. Evidence at every step.
howItWorks.body: Each stage produces the evidence and decisions the next one needs. We don't jump into action before we understand your business, your objectives and what success looks like, because action without direction is how the money got wasted last time.

stages.title: The Business Now
stages.body: How you and your team see the business today: goals, customers, business model, capacity, risks, and where you personally want to end up. That last one matters more than most consultants admit.

stages.title: The Opportunity
stages.body: We test the assumptions against customer research, real numbers and market reality. Some will hold up. Some won't. Either way, you'll know instead of wondering. Then we put a value on each opportunity and rank them by what they're worth.

stages.section: A clearer place in the market
stages.title: Branding & Positioning
stages.body: What you're really selling, the problem you solve, why the right customers should choose you, and how you stand apart in a way you can actually deliver on.

stages.section: Who matters and how to reach them
stages.title: Audiences, Messaging & Channel Planning
stages.body: Which customers matter most, who decides and who influences, what to say to each of them, and the best way to reach them. No spray, no pray.

stages.title: Go To Market & Implementation
stages.body: A staged plan: who does what, when, what it costs, and how you'll know it's working. Plus the tools your team needs to run it without us.

intro.heading: The problem
body: Most new businesses create a logo and build the website first. Then they wonder why it isn't bringing in work.

A logo and a site are just pretty outputs; they help people recognise your business (eventually) and understand what you do if they visit the site. They only work when they express a decision you have already made - who you are for (customers), what you are really selling (what problem you are solving for them), and why someone should choose you over the alternative.
LAUNCH makes those decisions first, then builds everything to match.

hero.title: From the real problem - to work that performs.
hero.body: We work from business objectives and problem definition through to delivery. Take one phase or the whole journey.

howWeWork.intro: Some organisations need help defining the problem. Some have a clear brief but need strategy and direction. Some need ongoing guidance to make sure execution stays true to the strategic intent.

phases.title: Understand
phases.tagline: We identify the problem underneath the surface
phases.body: Before any strategy work begins we need to understand what is really going on. Audience research, stakeholder insight, communications audits and strategic analysis, to define the real challenge rather than the symptoms.
phases.approach: Can run as a standalone diagnostic or as the foundation for everything that follows. The diagnostic output becomes the objectives and success measures.

phases.title: Strategise
phases.tagline: We turn complexity into a clear plan.
phases.body: Once the objectives are clear we build the strategy: the frameworks, plans and direction that guide decisions, shape creative development and keep activity aligned to outcomes.
phases.approach: Delivered as a complete plan, or built alongside your internal team to develop capability. Every strategy is designed to survive contact with reality.

phases.title: Assemble and direct
phases.tagline: We help the strategy survive contact with reality.
phases.body: Strategy only works if it is executed well. We help you identify and brief the right specialist partners, provide oversight during implementation, and keep the work true to the original intent.
delivers: Internal team support and capability building
phases.approach: This is where the tailored team model comes to life: technology, creative, media, content producers, delivery teams and anything else the strategy needs, selected for the job rather than because they are already on the books.

phases.title: Measure
phases.tagline: We help you understand what worked and what to do next.
phases.body: Measuring outcomes is how we learn. Evaluate performance, test messages, review what worked, and plan refinements on evidence rather than instinct.
phases.approach: Evaluation feeds back into strategy, building a cycle of learning that makes future work sharper.

cta.title: Strategy through to delivery.
cta.body: We work from problem definition through to identifying, briefing and guiding the right execution partners.

hero.title: Start with the right questions. Then build the right response.
hero.paraA: Independent counsel for government, brands and complex organisations, before the money goes into campaigns, content or creative.
hero.supportLine: So the decision holds up before the budget moves, not after it's been spent.
hero.paraB: We help you define your objectives, understand the real problem, shape the strategy that answers it, and brief the right specialists to deliver it.

theCase.title: Most briefs describe a symptom.
theCase.paraA: By the time a brief reaches a marketing team or supplier, the problem has usually been defined by whoever wrote it, and the response is shaped by whatever the marketing team is set up to deliver or that supplier happens to sell.
theCase.paraB: We work upstream of that. What are the business objectives? What is the organisation actually trying to change? Who has to behave differently for it to happen? Where is influence genuinely available, and where is it being spent for no return?
theCase.paraC: Only then does it make sense to talk about what the work should be.
theCase.paraD: The result is an answer you can take into the room that has to approve it, with the reasoning already attached.

theDifference.title: Structurally independent.
theDifference.paraA: We don't keep a fixed team. We build the right people around each challenge, bringing together specialist partners based on what the work needs, not what we happen to have in-house.
theDifference.paraB: No permanent team. No payroll to feed. No preferred answer waiting for a question.
theDifference.paraC: And we stay through delivery. Strategy that isn't carried into execution isn't strategy. It's a document.

index.title: Case studies
index.paraA: Selected work across government, behaviour change, brand strategy and product launches, including some of Australia's largest brands and most complex stakeholder environments. The budgets differ enormously. The growth principles underneath them do not.
index.paraB: Every one of these started with a brief that described a symptom. The work was finding what was actually holding growth back.

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Korean brands were competing hard on price and winning. Toyota was being pulled into a price-and-discounting war it could not win without discounting its way down, eroding brand value and reducing margins for the factory and dealers.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: The brief focused on price and on making dealers feel that the factory was supporting them in the face of increased competition. The research said price was the wrong battleground entirely. A national research program with consumers and dealers found that people define value as the whole ownership experience: reliability, servicing, running costs, resale, not the number on the windscreen. So the work was to move the conversation from price to value: the number on the windscreen is not what the car costs you. Toyota was already winning that argument. It just was not having it.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Ran the national research program with consumers and dealers
Built the 'A Lifetime of Advantages' positioning and marketing plan from the findings
Rolled it across brand, retail, finance and service communications
Made the proposition consistent wherever a customer encountered Toyota

result.heading: The result
result.headline: Market share grew from 17% to 22% in twelve months.
result.body: The platform outlasted the campaign and remained central to Toyota communications for years afterwards.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Nobody grows by discounting. Growth under price pressure comes from knowing what your customers are actually buying and saying it out loud, the same move whether you run five dealerships or five hundred.

cta.title: If price feels like the only lever left, that's worth testing before you pull it.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to grow, and let's book a call or grab a coffee.

ford-six-model-launches.title: Ford: Six Model Launches in Six Months
ford-six-model-launches.attribution: National advertising and launch planning lead

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Ford was refreshing its entire model line-up, six new vehicles to market in six months, into a slowing category with new competitors arriving regularly. The dealer network needed to see the factory behind them, with product that gave them an edge on the floor.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: Six launches is not one problem six times. Run separately, they compete for attention, budget and dealer energy, and the weakest one drags the rest down. The work was a single consistent voice that each launch built on and local dealers could use, then sequencing and proportion across the six. Not six campaigns.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Created the unifying 'Ford, Of Course' brand positioning as the halo for all campaigns nationally, regionally and locally
Built national advertising and promotional plans across all six launches as one program
Managed a $100m+ budget through a highly competitive market period
Targeted each launch to the right audience for the right reason rather than treating them alike
Moved Ford from a wholly broadcast media strategy into one-to-one channels: digital, direct and sponsorship, including Cricket Australia

result.heading: The result
result.headline: FG Falcon became Ford's most successful launch since 2000.
result.body: Market share held above 13% through the period, and all six launches delivered, with Ranger and FG Falcon carrying the program.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Whether you are launching six models or two services, the constraint is the same: you always have more to promote than there is attention to spend on it. Deciding what leads, what follows and what waits, and making it all sound like one business, is worth more than doing all of it at once, badly.

cta.title: Got more you want to launch than attention to spend on it? That's a sequencing problem, not a budget one.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to grow, and let's book a call or grab a coffee.

commbank-little-card-big-rewards.title: Commonwealth Bank: Little Card, Big Rewards

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Launch CBA's first cash-back credit card into a crowded market. The brief was simple and almost impossible: make people care about another credit card.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: Nobody wants a credit card. They want the thing the credit card does. Category language, rates, rewards, points, tiers, was making a genuinely simple benefit sound complicated, and complicated products do not get applied for.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Built a campaign that was clear, cheeky and plainly spoken
Explained cashback as money back, in language people grasped immediately
Deliberately avoided sounding like a bank
Made the value obvious from the first interaction rather than the fine print

result.heading: The result
result.headline: Online applications rose 30% after launch.
result.body: A national campaign built around one easily understood idea.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Every extra sentence needed to explain what you sell costs you customers before price is ever discussed. Clarity is not a creative flourish: it is the cheapest growth lever most businesses never pull.

cta.title: If your product needs more than a sentence to explain, that's the first thing worth fixing.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to grow, and let's book a call or grab a coffee.

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: A brand extension into an already crowded popcorn category. It had to feel new enough to be worth noticing, and familiar enough to still be Kettle.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: Brand extensions usually fail in one of two directions, too different and the equity does not transfer, too similar and there is no reason to buy. The real task was working out precisely which parts of Kettle were doing the work, and holding onto exactly those.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Developed the go-to-market plan for the launch
Built positioning and messaging around a premium tone with a slightly irreverent edge
Kept the proposition grounded in product truth rather than category cliché
Shaped execution so the product felt distinctive and recognisably Kettle, and linked directly back to Kettle's foundations as premium snacks

result.heading: The result
result.headline: The most successful brand extension launch in Snack Brands' history.
result.body: Ranging secured in Coles, Woolworths, Metcash and independents.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Extending the range is the most common growth move at any size, and the most commonly botched. Growth comes from the part of your reputation that already works, the trick is knowing which part, and holding onto exactly that.

cta.title: Thinking about a brand extension? Let's work out which parts of what you have are actually doing the work.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to grow, and let's book a call or grab a coffee.

state-election-2022.title: 2022 South Australian State Election
state-election-2022.attribution: Strategic lead, Electoral Commission of South Australia

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Three major electoral events approaching, participation declining, COVID pressures mounting and voter fatigue building after a federal election.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: ECSA engaged us to help procure an advertising supplier. Within weeks, it was clear that was not the problem. The communications function itself was not working: no strategic framework, no crisis capability, and no way for a new supplier to succeed even if one were appointed. They did not need a better supplier. They needed a function that understood the business objectives, who the audience was, the challenges and opportunities and how to deliver, in a tight time frame with high public scrutiny and reputational risk.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Delivered a full capability review and identified the structural gaps
Built a multi-year strategy aligned to operational realities and government obligations
Developed organisational capability, supported by the right external partners
Established the media engagement and crisis communications framework from scratch
Ran statewide research to identify audience segments, behavioural barriers and channel needs
Directed strategy, creative, media, PR and crisis communications through to implementation

result.heading: The result
result.headline: 92% participation maintained through COVID conditions and voter fatigue.
result.body: Targeted engagement reached CALD communities, young people and disengaged voters.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Growth spend fails most often because the thing being bought is not the thing needed. Diagnosis before procurement is not a delay, it is what makes the money work.

cta.title: Not sure the thing you're about to buy is actually the thing you need? That's worth a conversation first.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to shift. We'll come back to you within one business day.

local-government-elections-2022.title: 2022 Local Government Elections
local-government-elections-2022.attribution: Campaign strategy lead, Electoral Commission of South Australia

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Council elections are voluntary and participation has declined at every election in the last 25 years. With participation around 30% for years, and some districts below 15%, maintaining and growing turnout was critical for public confidence in the process and electoral integrity. They also fell in the same calendar year as two major parliamentary elections, so there were high levels of voter fatigue and disinterest in local government.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: This was not an awareness problem, it was a relevance problem: people didn't see the relevance of local councils in their daily lives, so had no motivation to vote. And the mechanism: postal voting asks people to complete and return a ballot themselves, a different behaviour with more steps and more places to give up. Telling more people about the election would not have moved it; we needed to create relevance and tell people what to do.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Built an integrated campaign across enrolment, nominations and voting rather than one message
Created relevance for the audience by focusing on what councils did for them, councils are more than rates, roads and rubbish
Built awareness of timing and responsibilities, not just the event
Encouraged business and non-citizen enrolment and promoted early completion and return of ballots
Coordinated messaging across ECSA, councils and the LGA

result.heading: The result
result.headline: Participation lifted from 30% to over 34%, a gain of more than 13% increase against a long-term decline, the first time participation had increased in over 25 years.
result.body: First-week postal ballot returns rose by 300%, improving processing efficiency and delivering results faster.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Growth comes from people acting, not from people noticing. Most marketing that fails has bought the attention and skipped the step that turns it into behaviour.

cta.title: Getting people to notice and getting them to act are two different jobs. Let's talk about which one you're missing.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to shift. We'll come back to you within one business day.

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: The Adelaide Hills is one of Australia's leading cool-climate wine regions: 70 km of ridges and valleys, 90+ winemakers, 50+ cellar doors. The region is widely respected but lacks a story about itself, a shared focus or a consistent brand to unite behind.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: The brief was to develop a brand positioning, but the real problem was internal: members, while united in the need for a coherent story, couldn't agree on who the region was, who it competed against, or what it should say to consumers, visitors, government, industry bodies and sponsors. Everyone was focused on their own business rather than growing the region as a whole and making the pie bigger for everyone. No amount of positioning work survives that. Agreement had to come first.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Ran the largest qualitative and quantitative research program ever undertaken for an Australian wine region, covering consumers, stakeholders, industry and government, at local, national and international levels
Clarified who the region was, what it stood for, where it was heading and why anyone should believe it
Defined how the region should talk about itself in a way that united members rather than dividing them
Built the brand positioning, architecture and communications strategy, positioning the Adelaide Hills as the first choice for Australian cool-climate wine

result.heading: The result
result.headline: A research-led positioning and a clear regional narrative, agreed by members.
result.body: A shared platform for visitation, partnerships, government engagement and events, and a road map the region can act on: defined audiences, messages, beliefs and personality that positioned the region for growth.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: If the people inside a business cannot agree on what it is, that's where we'd start too. No marketing or communications strategy will settle it. That agreement is the first thing the Growth Program goes looking for, because everything you spend afterwards depends on it.

cta.title: If the people inside your business can't agree on what it is, that's where we'd start too.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to grow, and let's book a call or grab a coffee.

first-nations-voice-2024.title: 2024 First Nations Voice to Parliament Election
first-nations-voice-2024.attribution: Communications strategy lead, Electoral Commission of South Australia

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: South Australia's first First Nations Voice election, held after the failed national Voice Referendum, with 46 positions up for election across six regions, held on 16 March 2024. Originally scheduled for September 2023 and moved to avoid overlapping the Federal Voice Referendum.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: Confusion, public resentment, and a lack of understanding across the community as to what it was, how it worked and what it meant to them. Standard election advertising was never going to carry this. A new electoral process, communities spread across six regions, and a timing change that had already disrupted understanding. Reach was not the constraint; trust and comprehension were.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Identified early that conventional advertising alone would not work, and built a community-led approach instead
Combined communications strategy, community engagement, media engagement, advertising, PR and budget management
Delivered across statewide direct community engagement with the community, supported by TV, press, outdoor, digital, website, social and PR
Created more than 500 community engagement kits and supported over 400 engagement sessions

result.heading: The result
result.headline: All 46 positions attracted multiple nominations.
result.body: Not one was filled uncontested, and elections were successfully held across every position, establishing the credibility of First Nations Voice to SA Parliament and delivering the stakeholders' objectives and success measures.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: When the people you need are not reachable through the obvious channels, spending more there does not buy growth. Going where they already are does, and that is true at any budget.

cta.title: When the obvious channels aren't reaching the people you need, that's a strategy problem before it's a media-buying one.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to shift. We'll come back to you within one business day.
